Sources: verification/catalogue/pages/functional-queue.md (its sources: list is the backbone), research/mastery-20260927/demos-data-structures.md §6.2, definitions-lemmas.md §1-2, INDEX.md on unreachable_; every claim re-checked against the code at 8479634adc.
_notes: contents is runtime code (reverse_append then append) and is not in collections_boundary_check.ml's audit list; only enqueue and dequeue are. The interface exports contents but not contents_def, so clients learn contents only through the three operations' refinements.
title: The functional queue
summary: `Functional_queue` is the two-list persistent queue: a front list and a reversed rear list. Its interface describes every queue by `contents`, the list of its elements, so a client reasons about a queue as a list. The tour is short: the interface and the list vocabulary it uses, a client and a rejected client, then the representation, the reversal lemma, the proof of `dequeue` and the check that the compiled operations run no proof code.
The [catalogue page](demo:functional-queue) states the claim, the trusted base and the scope, including what is not proved: running time.

stops.title: The interface: a queue is its contents
stops.text: `t` is abstract, and `contents` is its only observation, declared `@@ total` so that refinements may mention it. The refinement of `empty` says its contents are `[]`, and `enqueue` appends `[value]` at the end. `dequeue` takes a queue refined by `(contents q === []) === false`, a nonempty queue, and returns a pair whose head and tail's contents rebuild `contents q`. The interface exports no equation for `contents` itself: a client knows the contents of a queue only through these three refinements, which determine it for every queue a client can build. Elements must be `immutable_data`, which excludes closures and records with mutable fields.

stops.title: The list vocabulary: append and its equation
stops.text: `Vox_sequence.t` is `'a list`, and `append` is list concatenation, declared total. The solver sees `append` as an uninterpreted function: it knows nothing about it until a proof calls `append_def`, just below, whose type is the defining equation, generated from `let[@def] rec append` in the implementation. `append_associative` and `append_nil` are exported the same way, as total functions whose result types are the laws. This is the whole of the logic the queue's contract uses beyond OCaml lists and `===`.

stops.title: A client proof: first in, first out
stops.text: `fifo` enqueues two values, dequeues twice and proves that they come out in order and that the queue is empty again. The refinements of `enqueue`'s results are facts about `q1` and `q2`, from which the checker proves each `dequeue`'s precondition and the result type. It does not evaluate `append` on its own: the three `append_def` calls in `ghost_` unfold it once each, so that `append [] [first]` is known to be `[first]`. The `let () =` below instantiates `fifo` at `int`, at a record type and at `int list`, and runs as bytecode and native code.

stops.title: A rejected client: dequeue from the empty queue
stops.text: Passing `empty` to `dequeue` is a type error. The test compiles only the two interfaces, with `-principal`, and requires the error in [`queue_rejected.compilers.reference`](src:testsuite/tests/vox/queue_rejected.compilers.reference): the refinement could not be proved, with a counterexample, and the refinement is the one stated in `functional_queue.mli` on `dequeue`'s argument. `collections_boundary.ml` rejects a variant that first ascribes the nonempty type to `empty`, and one that reads the hidden field `front`.

stops.title: Inside: two lists and what they mean
stops.from: type ('a : immutable_data) t = {front : 'a list; rear : 'a list}
stops.text: The representation is a record of two lists, and there is no representation invariant: every `{front; rear}` is a valid queue, including one with an empty front and a nonempty rear. `contents` is both the specification and runtime code. It computes `reverse_append q.rear []` and appends it to the front, and its `ghost_` call relates that to the naive `reverse`. `contents_model` states the model the proofs use, `contents q === append q.front (reverse q.rear)`, by unfolding `contents` with `contents_def`. `contents` takes time linear in the queue, and it is the only way a client can test emptiness at run time.

stops.title: The key lemma: the fast reverse is the naive one
stops.text: The specification uses the quadratic `reverse`, whose equation is easy to reason about; the code uses the accumulator loop `reverse_append`. `reverse_append_correct` bridges them, `reverse_append xs acc === append (reverse xs) acc`, by induction on `xs`: the recursive call is the hypothesis for `tail` with `head :: acc`, and `append_associative` regroups `append (append rest [head]) acc`. Each `_def` call unfolds one definition at one argument; nothing is unfolded automatically. `reverse` itself never runs: it appears only in `ghost_` code and refinements.

stops.title: The core proof: dequeue, and an unreachable branch
stops.text: `dequeue` assumes its argument's refinement, that `contents q` is not `[]`. When the front is nonempty the proof is `contents_model` for the old and the new queue. When it is empty, the code reverses the rear with `reverse_append`, and the `ghost_` block relates the result to `reverse original.rear`, which is `contents q` when the front is empty. The branch where that reversal is `[]` ends in `unreachable_ ()`, a proof obligation: the checker must show that the branch is dead, here because the contents are nonempty, and the compiled code keeps a trap there. `let reversed = ghost_ (reverse original.rear)` binds a ghost value, available to proofs and erased from the code.

stops.title: Erasure: the operations run no proof code
stops.text: [`collections_boundary.ml`](src:testsuite/tests/vox/collections_boundary.ml) compiles `functional_queue.ml` with `-dlambda` under both compilers, with and without `-principal`, and this check requires that the bodies of `enqueue` and `dequeue` call no `_def` equation and none of `contents`, `reverse` and `reverse_append_correct`. The demo trusts nothing beyond the shared base: the implementation contains no `assume_` or `external`, and the one `unreachable_ ()` is proved. What is not proved is cost: when a version is dequeued more than once, the rear list can be reversed more than once, and no amortized bound is stated.
